sar.narrative: This report documents suspected card-not-present payment fraud involving the deliberate structuring of online purchase amounts just below a $500 authorization threshold on card C07297-K1, issued to customer C07297. On 2016-11-21 between 20:00 and 20:30, four online purchases of the same product type (product C) were authorized on the card: transaction 3476602 for $478.95 at 20:00, transaction 3476633 for $456.96 at 20:10, transaction 3476665 for $488.04 at 20:24, and transaction 3476682 for $482.12 at 20:30, totaling $1,906.07. Customer C07297 contacted the bank and disputed transaction 3476682, the last of the four purchases. All four transactions were flagged as originating from a device that was new to the account, and they were spread across two distinct device strings, two different email domains (gmail.com and yahoo.com), with two of the four routed through a transparent proxy. The card's 180-day baseline shows 199 transactions, of which 194 were in person and only 5 online (2.5 percent online share), with product C appearing only three times (1.5 percent) and a mean transaction value of $116.73; each episode amount is approximately 3.9 to 4.2 times that mean, with an amount z-score of 2.71. Legitimate in-person activity on the same card continued in the cardholder's home regions before, during and after the online burst, including transaction 3474057 for $226.02 in region 264 and transaction 3477578 for $82.97 in region 315 at 02:07 on 2016-11-22, indicating that the card number was being used online in parallel with the genuine cardholder's physical use. The activity is suspicious because the amounts were consistently shaved just under a round $500 authorization limit, the purchases were compressed into a 30-minute window on a card that is overwhelmingly used in person, and credentials and devices were rotated across each attempt, which is consistent with scripted abuse of authorization limits rather than ordinary customer behavior. A review of shared devices found no rare shared-device link, and the newcomer fraud rate for region 264 (0.10) equals the base rate, so no shared-origin ring was identified. The total exposure is $1,906.07. The bank blocked card C07297-K1, opened a fraud case, filed this report because exposure exceeds $1,000 and the pattern is not one of the institution's documented typologies, and escalated the matter to an analyst for further investigation.

stop_reason: Fraud probability 0.89 supported by five independent signals (dispute, 4-txn threshold-shaving burst, off-baseline channel/product/amount, New-device and proxy/email rotation, continuing home activity); §6 stopping condition met.
